registrySplitMeasurement.question: Is the campaign host registry the probe route would read (Next API module graph) the same instance the socket runtime (tsx graph loaded by server.js:446-464) records CampaignAck into?
registrySplitMeasurement.answer: SPLIT. Two registry instances of two different class objects each hold an entry for the same live match. The API graph entry retains no participant and its evaluateScenarioLaunch() answers ok:true at every sample; the socket graph entry retains both guests and answers participants-behind while they trail the head. A probe route reading the API graph would report every head as converged.
method: Ran the ladder group as the charter says: machine-idle MACHINE_IDLE first; HOSTNAME=127.0.0.1 (process-scoped); NODE_ENV=production node scripts/qc/run-gm-two-player-campaign.mjs --group=performance; run id qc-performance, port 23319 from deriveFixturePort.

Resolved the webServer PID from the LISTENING socket on 23319 (pid 25956, cwd the worktree), activated its inspector with process._debugProcess(pid), and evaluated one read-only expression over the DevTools protocol (Runtime.evaluate) while the co-op session was live. No repository file was edited and no extra build was made for the measurement.
Socket graph: the Module._cache entry for src/lib/multiplayer/server/CampaignHostRegistry.ts (loaded through tsx by server.js), exports.getCampaignHostRegistry().

API graph: .next/server/webpack-api-runtime.js exports the webpack require (it keeps no public module cache); require(45433) is CampaignHostRegistry.ts in this build (export gH = getCampaignHostRegistry, located in .next/server/pages/api/multiplayer/matches.js at the class body that throws "Campaign snapshot revision is stale"). The webpack require returns the already-cached exports, so this is the instance src/pages/api/multiplayer/matches/index.ts:325 registered into and the one every API route sharing that runtime file (the probe route included) reads.

Per graph: registry entries (matchId, campaignId), the sync session retained map (acknowledged, delivered) and evaluateScenarioLaunch(); plus === on the two registries, their prototypes and the per-match sync sessions.

blocker.summary: The probe route cannot answer the authority's convergence: the registry it reads (API graph) is not the one the socket runtime records acknowledgements into. The fix is in src/lib/multiplayer/server, outside U86's ownership paths, so U86 stops BLOCKED at admission as its amended behaviour sentence directs.

successor.what: The campaign host registry held in a globalThis slot, as MatchHostRegistry does since U22a (MatchHostRegistry.ts:220-260)

replaceWith: type GlobalCampaignHostRegistrySlot = typeof globalThis & { [CAMPAIGN_HOST_REGISTRY_SLOT_KEY]?: CampaignHostRegistry | null };

/** The process registry, created on first use and held on globalThis, so Next's API graph (the match create route, the E2E probe) and the socket runtime's tsx graph (bindCampaignSyncConnection) read the same instance. */
if (!registry) { registry = new CampaignHostRegistry(); global[CAMPAIGN_HOST_REGISTRY_SLOT_KEY] = registry; }
/** Closes every entry and empties the slot (tests). */

behaviourToWeigh: MEASURED: today the socket graph holds its own entry for the match the create route registered in the API graph.
READ (CampaignHostRegistry.ts:351-387, :334-340): the socket side reaches its entry through getOrCreate, which registers with { rebuilt: true } and so calls pauseUntilGmReturns().

INFERENCE (not measured): with one shared registry the socket side would find the create route's entry (not rebuilt, not paused), and that entry's host, sync session and arbiter would be objects built from the API graph's module copies with their own module-level state (for example registerActiveCoopHost and the durable readers). That is why the successor is authority class and not a routine e2e change.
Once it lands, U86 needs no edit outside its paths: the probe route reads getCampaignHostRegistry().get(matchId)?.syncSession.evaluateScenarioLaunch() behind its existing guard.

designAnswers.probeRoute: Today it answers { success, wallMs, monotonicMs, memory: { rss, heapUsed } } only (src/pages-modules/api/e2ePerformanceProbeRoute.ts:23-33 type, :41-62 handler, guard :65-70; src/pages/api/e2e/performance-probe.ts:7 re-exports it). It carries no acknowledged revision. The amended paths let U86 add a matchId read of evaluateScenarioLaunch(), but MEASURED above: from the API graph that read answers ok:true with no retained participant, so the amendment alone cannot deliver the behaviour.
designAnswers.convergedMeansToTheAuthority: Only AdvanceDay is gated (bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:748-758 -> refuseUnconvergedProgression :700-718 -> CampaignSyncSession.evaluateScenarioLaunch :753-777). requiredRevision = max(0, nextSequence()-1), read live (:785-787). Clause refusals run first (:755-760), then every RETAINED participant must have acknowledged >= requiredRevision (:761-770). Retained = non-GM participants (joinMember :520-531 and retainHydratedParticipant :430-439 skip the host). acknowledged rises only through noteParticipantAcknowledged (:660-671), called from the CampaignAck dispatch (bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:619-626) and refused above the delivered watermark (:667). MEASURED live: the socket graph retained exactly two participant ids, never three.
designAnswers.convergeWaitToday: converge() at e2e/gm-two-player-performance.pack.spec.ts:630-646: max painted head across the three pages, polls each page's appliedSequence (set on frame receipt, :511) for up to functionalWaitMs*5, then a fixed 25 ms (:644). Call sites :165 (warm-up) and :198 (measured). The tail builder (:268-272) uses waitForSequence only (:271). waitForSequence :596-614 (called :173, :206, :271) is the 2,000 ms functional wait. READ: the client transport hands a frame to onFrame listeners (campaignSyncTransport.ts:228) before it sends CampaignAck (:244), so appliedSequence reaches the head before the ack leaves the page.
designAnswers.gmTransportRefusal: The refusal is an Error frame { kind: 'Error', code: 'CAMPAIGN_NOT_CONVERGED', reason: 'participants-behind <id>:<ack>,...; requiredRevision N', intentId } (bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:708-716; errorFrame :1550-1564; CampaignProgressionGate.ts:195-206; schema src/types/multiplayer/Protocol.ts:807). The GM transport passes every parsed frame, Error included, to onFrame listeners (campaignSyncTransport.ts:228), and the pack's intentId is perf-<kind>-<ordinal> (controlledLoopbackFixture.ts:296). A GM-page onFrame capture keyed by intentId is a real read and needs no edit outside e2e. Not built in this attempt: admission stopped first.
